cardboard_box.reason: Flatten clean cardboard; bundle oversized pieces beside the cart.
cardboard_box.quote: Cardboard • Flattened cardboard • Extra or oversized cardboard

pizza_box_greasy.reason: Greasy pizza boxes go in the green compost cart.
pizza_box_greasy.quote: Fiber-based (bamboo, wood) utensils • Greasy pizza boxes

paper_mixed.reason: Clean paper and mail go in the blue recycling cart.
paper_mixed.quote: Paper, cardboard, glass, aluminum/tin cans, rigid plastics, and bagged film plastics such as bags & bubble wrap go into the blue recyclable cart.

paperboard_box.reason: Recycle the box; remove the plastic liner first.
paperboard_box.quote: Cereal and cracker boxes (plastic liners removed)

paper_bag.reason: Clean paper bags go in recycling.

shredded_paper.reason: Bag shredded paper first, then put it in recycling.
shredded_paper.quote: Shredded paper (in a clear plastic bag, tied closed)
shredded_paper.note: Official sources differ on the bag: Recology's 2025-26 guide says a clear plastic bag; the City's recycling FAQ says a paper bag. Both say bag it and recycle it, so the reason doesn't pick one.

paper_towel_napkin.reason: Used paper towels and napkins go in compost.
paper_towel_napkin.quote: Paper bags, napkins, towels, cups, and plates

tissue.reason: Used tissues go in the compost cart.
tissue.quote: Please place in compost cart: Food contaminated paper packaging Paper towels Napkins Tissue

paper_cup.reason: Food-soiled paper cups go in the compost cart.
paper_cup.quote: Paper bags, napkins, towels, cups, and plates

paper_plate_used.reason: Food-soiled paper plates go in the compost cart.
paper_plate_used.quote: Paper bags, napkins, towels, cups, and plates

paper_takeout.reason: Compost paper take-out boxes without plastic lining.

carton.note: Official sources disagree. Recology's Nov 2025 sorting guide lists cartons under RECYCLE, but the City's compost page lists 'Milk Cartons' and its recycling FAQ says milk/other cartons go in the compost cart (both still live, Oct 2026).

aseptic_carton.note: Official sources disagree. Recology's 2025-26 guide lists 'Aseptic containers' under the Recycle Cart, but the City's recycling FAQ says milk/other cartons go in the compost cart.

receipt.note: Not listed in Recology's Cupertino guides or pages.

coffee_grounds_filter.reason: Coffee grounds and paper filters go in compost.
coffee_grounds_filter.quote: Coffee filter and paper tea bags

tea_bag.reason: Paper tea bags go in the compost cart.
tea_bag.quote: Coffee filter and paper tea bags

book.reason: Paperback and hardcover books go in recycling.

plastic_bottle.reason: Empty plastic bottles go in the blue cart.

plastic_jug.reason: Empty plastic jugs go in the blue cart.

plastic_tub.reason: Empty, scraped plastic tubs go in recycling.

plastic_clamshell.reason: Plastic containers go in recycling; empty and clean.

plastic_cup.reason: Empty cold-drink plastic cups, then put them in the blue recycling cart.
plastic_cup.quote: Yes, cold liquid plastic cups can be placed into the recycling.

also.quote: All recyclables should be empty, clean, and dry before they are placed in the blue bin.

plastic_takeout.reason: Plastic containers go in recycling; scrape out food.

plastic_bag.reason: Bundle clean, dry bags into one tied bag, then recycle.
plastic_bag.quote: Recology is still accepting plastic bags in the recycling, but they must be clean, dry, and bundled into one plastic bag and tied.

bubble_wrap.reason: Bag bubble wrap with other clean film, then blue cart.
bubble_wrap.quote: Bubble wrap and other clean, dry plastic bags and film plastic (bagged)

plastic_utensils.reason: Plastic utensils go in the landfill cart.

straw.reason: Straws go in the landfill cart.

snack_wrapper.reason: Chip bags and wrappers go in the landfill cart.
snack_wrapper.quote: Chip bags, candy, granola bar wrappers, dirty plastics, and dirty foil

compostable_plastic.reason: "Compostable" plastics go in landfill, not compost.

foam_food_container.reason: Foam and polystyrene go in the landfill cart.

foam_packaging.reason: Foam packing and peanuts go in the landfill cart.
foam_packaging.quote: packing peanuts, meat trays, and other packing material

plastic_cap.note: Not addressed for loose caps. The City's FAQ says caps should be left on bottles and jars when recycling them.

coffee_pod.note: Not listed in Recology's Cupertino guides or pages.

drink_pouch.note: Not listed in Recology's Cupertino guides or pages.

toothpaste_tube.note: Not listed in Recology's Cupertino guides or pages.

toothbrush.note: Not listed in Recology's Cupertino guides or pages.

plastic_toy.note: Guides list plastic containers only; toys not addressed.

aluminum_can.reason: Empty aluminum cans go in the blue cart.

food_can.reason: Empty, scraped metal cans go in recycling.

aluminum_foil.reason: Recycle foil only if it has no food on it.

aluminum_tray.note: Guide lists foil and cans; trays and pie tins not addressed.

aerosol_can.quote: Glass and Metal • Empty aerosol cans

glass_bottle.reason: Empty glass bottles go in the blue cart.

glass_jar.reason: Empty, scraped glass jars go in recycling.

broken_glass.reason: Broken glass goes in the landfill cart.
broken_glass.quote: Pet waste, snack wrappers, straws, ceramics, ashes, and broken glass to name a few.

drinking_glass.note: Guide lists glass bottles and jars only.

ceramic.reason: Ceramics go in the landfill cart.
ceramic.quote: Pet waste, snack wrappers, straws, ceramics, ashes, and broken glass to name a few.

food_scraps.reason: Food scraps go in the green compost cart.
food_scraps.quote: Food scraps, food-soiled paper, and yard trimmings (such as grass, branches, and plants) go in the green compost cart.

bones.reason: Meat scraps, including bones, go in the compost cart.
bones.quote: Fruit, including pits Meat, including bones

yard_trimmings.reason: Leaves, grass and branches go in the compost cart.

flowers.reason: Flowers and floral trimmings go in compost.

cooking_oil.reason: Set out sealed cooking-oil jugs with your carts on collection day.
cooking_oil.quote: Sealed used motor oil and cooking oil jugs

wooden_chopsticks.reason: Wood and bamboo utensils go in the compost cart.

battery.reason: Tape ends, seal in clear bag, set on recycling cart.
battery.quote: Place household batteries in a sealed clear bag on top of the recyclables cart, tape battery ends before bagging.

phone_electronics.reason: Illegal in carts; free Recology on-call pickup: 408-725-4020.
phone_electronics.quote: It is against the law to place e-waste in your garbage or recycling containers.

cords_cables.note: Cords are not named on Recology's Cupertino e-waste list.

bulb_fluorescent.reason: Sealed bag on top of recycling cart, or drop off via hhw.org.
bulb_fluorescent.quote: For compact bulbs (CFLs) and linear, circular, spiral and U-bent tubes: Place them in a sealed plastic bag on top of your blue recycling cart

bulb_led.reason: Hazardous waste: book free drop-off at hhw.org.
bulb_led.quote: HHW includes paint, cleaners, pesticides, light bulbs, propane, batteries, etc.

bulb_incandescent.note: Guide lists 'light bulbs' under HHW without saying which types; not stated for incandescent.

paint.reason: Free PaintCare take-back, or book drop-off at hhw.org.
paint.quote: PaintCare offers take-back programs at no charge.

cleaning_product.reason: Cleaners are hazardous waste: book free drop-off at hhw.org.
cleaning_product.quote: HHW includes paint, cleaners, pesticides, light bulbs, propane, batteries, etc.

medicine.reason: Never trash; drop off or mail back via med-project.org.
medicine.quote: Find drop-off locations and mail-back supplies for medication and sharps at med-project.org

sharps.reason: Illegal in carts; seal in biohazard container, use take-back.
sharps.quote: California law prohibits the disposal of “sharps waste” in trash or recycling containers.

propane_cylinder.reason: Hazardous waste: book free drop-off at hhw.org.
propane_cylinder.quote: HHW includes paint, cleaners, pesticides, light bulbs, propane, batteries, etc.

diaper.reason: Diapers go in the landfill cart.

pet_waste.reason: Pet waste goes in the landfill cart.

kitty_litter.reason: Cat litter goes in the landfill cart.

face_mask.reason: Disposable masks go in the landfill cart.

disposable_gloves.reason: Disposable gloves go in the landfill cart.

textiles.reason: Textiles, leather and hangers go in the landfill cart.

shoes.note: Shoes are not named in Recology's Cupertino guides.

cigarette.note: Not listed in Recology's Cupertino guides or pages.

wipes.note: Not listed in Recology's Cupertino guides or pages.

garden_hose.reason: Garden hoses go in the landfill cart.

egg_carton_paper.note: Not listed in the 2025-26 Cupertino guide.

egg_carton_foam.reason: Foam and polystyrene go in the landfill cart.

frozen_food_box.reason: Wax-lined frozen food boxes go in the landfill cart.
frozen_food_box.quote: NO frozen food boxes with wax lining- these go in the trash
frozen_food_box.exception: The quote is a parenthetical exclusion inside the Mixed Paper (recycling) list; it says these boxes go in the trash.

food_in_container.reason: Scrape the food into the compost cart first, then scan the empty container.
food_in_container.quote: Food scraps, food-soiled paper, and yard trimmings (such as grass, branches, and plants) go in the green compost cart.

also.quote: Got leftover food in a recyclable container? Step 1 - scrape the food out of the container and into the compost. Step 2 - recycle the container.
